policy.topic: Fee Waiver and Goodwill Credit Authority
policy.text:
# Internal Policy: Fee Waiver and Goodwill Credit Authority

**Applies to:** Complaints where account/transaction data confirms a fee was charged in error, or where a goodwill gesture is being considered for a confirmed service failure.

## Authority thresholds
| Fee/credit amount | Who may approve |
|---|---|
| $0 – $50 | Complaints analyst, no additional sign-off required |
| $50.01 – $200 | Complaints analyst with supervisor co-sign |
| $200.01+ | Supervisor or manager approval required; analyst may not approve independently |

## When a waiver is appropriate
- The transaction history **confirms** the fee was charged in error (e.g., payment was received before the due date but a late fee was still assessed).
- The fee was charged due to a documented system or processing error.
- A documented goodwill exception for a first-time, low-dollar fee on an otherwise good-standing account (use sparingly, document the rationale).

## When a waiver is NOT appropriate
- The transaction history confirms the fee was correctly charged (no error occurred) — the response should explain the charge, not waive it.
- The complaint's underlying fact could not be verified (missing/incomplete data) — route to manual review rather than waiving preemptively.
- The complaint involves a dispute of right vs. convenience (e.g., customer disagrees with a disclosed, legitimate fee) — explain the fee and its basis; do not waive solely to end the complaint.

## What an analyst or agent may say
- May state the exact dollar amount being waived and the specific reason (tied to the confirmed error).
- May NOT waive a fee "as a one-time courtesy" without a documented rationale on file — every waiver must cite either a confirmed error or an explicit goodwill justification.

## Documentation requirement
Every waiver, regardless of amount, must be logged with: the confirming evidence (which transaction record), the dollar amount, and the approving party.

*This is an internal, generic policy created for a training/demonstration environment and does not reflect any specific company's actual policy.*

draft.draft_text:
You contacted us about a $35 late fee that you believe was charged this month even though you paid on time. We understand how frustrating an unexpected charge can be, so we reviewed your account closely.

Here is what we found. Your payment of $180 was received on June 8, 2026, two days before your June 10, 2026 due date, so you are right that it arrived on time. We also found no late fee on your account for June, and no $35 charge appears anywhere in your transaction history.

You also mentioned that you pay the same way every month and this has never happened before. The records we reviewed show your June payment arrived on time and no late fee was assessed. Because no fee was charged, there is nothing to waive or refund.

If you are seeing a $35 charge on a statement or in your banking activity, please send us a copy or the details, such as the date and the description shown. We will review whatever you send us, and you are welcome to share more information at any time. You can reply to this message or call the number on your account.

Case reference: SYN-F01
draft.policy_cited: 06 Fee Waiver and Goodwill Credit Authority, 'When a waiver is NOT appropriate' (no fee was charged, so no waiver or credit applies)
allegations_addressed: Charged a $35 late fee this month despite paying on time
Pays the same way every month and this has never happened before

verifier.completeness_check: pass — both allegations are addressed: the $35 late fee despite on-time payment (findings and outcome paragraphs), and the claim that the customer pays the same way every month and this has never happened before (third paragraph).
verifier.groundedness_check: pass — the $180 payment on June 8, 2026, the June 10, 2026 due date, the absence of any June late fee, and the absence of any $35 charge in the transaction history all match the verification output. The statement that there is nothing to waive or refund follows from the confirmed absence of a fee. No invented facts, dates, or amounts.
verifier.policy_authorization_check: pass — the draft states no remedy (remedy_stated and referral_stated are null) and promises no waiver, refund, or credit. This is consistent with the Fee Waiver policy, which does not support a waiver when no fee was charged.
verifier.prohibited_language_check: pass — no fault admission (the draft confirms only that the payment was on time and no fee was assessed), no future guarantees, no legal conclusions, no unapproved promises, and nothing that discourages the customer from other channels. 'We understand how frustrating an unexpected charge can be' is the acceptable, non-performative acknowledgment Policy 10 allows.
verifier.tone_structure_check: pass — the draft follows Policy 11's order: specific acknowledgment, findings with dates and amounts, outcome (no fee charged, so nothing to waive or refund), next steps (send a statement copy or details, reply or call), then the case reference SYN-F01. It uses second person and plain language, short paragraphs, and has no marketing content. Length is acceptable for a multi-allegation complaint.
